BAS2-01.note: Fronting 'for the summer program' is marginal and unnatural without a comma.

alternatives: every player | expects | the coach | to bring | their own water bottle
BAS2-02.note: Subject/object swap. It is grammatical and plausible: 'their own' binds to the coach through singular they. The meaning changes, but it is a natural sentence.

alternatives: my grandfather | could convince | nobody | to replace | his old phone
BAS2-03.note: Swapping the two NPs gives 'My grandfather could convince nobody to replace his old phone', which is grammatical and coherent (he wanted someone else to replace it). 'could convince nobody' is slightly formal but acceptable.

BAS2-04.note: Fronting 'by a professional' is marginal. 'We' cannot move to object position.

BAS2-05.note: Topicalizing 'with the move she got her brother to help' is marginal.

BAS2-06.note: 'not only free' is one chip, so the halves cannot be swapped.

BAS2-08.note: Swapping 'anyone' and 'the second test' is nonsensical.

BAS2-10.note: Marginal: 'whether the store is still open I wonder' (topicalized, needs a comma to read naturally).

alternatives: why | the meeting | was cancelled | nobody | knows
BAS2-11.note: Topicalized embedded question: 'Why the meeting was cancelled nobody knows.' It is a standard, natural construction; a comma is customary but optional.

BAS2-12.note: Marginal: 'how the ancient bridge was built the guide explained' (topicalization, less natural than in 11).

BAS2-13.note: 'It was the lost keys who found my neighbor' is semantically absurd, and 'who' does not fit keys.

BAS2-15.note: Marginal or odd: 'learning the violin takes years of practice to play' and 'learning takes years of practice to play the violin'. Neither is natural.

alternatives: the instructor | must contact | students | who miss | the deadline
BAS2-18.note: Swapping the NPs gives 'The instructor must contact students who miss the deadline', which is fully grammatical and natural. The meaning changes.

BAS2-19.note: 'His manager did not satisfy the excuse that he offered' is semantically anomalous.

BAS2-22.note: 'The bacteria discovered that researchers could survive without oxygen' is grammatical but absurd.

alternatives: the speed | of the recovery | was | what | surprised | everyone
BAS2-23.note: Reversed pseudo-cleft: 'The speed of the recovery was what surprised everyone.' Fully natural.

BAS2-24.note: 'The weather depends on whether the plan will work' is grammatical but semantically absurd.

BAS2-25.note: Marginal: 'her handwriting almost is impossible to read'.

BAS2-28.note: 'Everyone made the long walk extremely hungry' is nonsensical.

BAS2-29.note: Moving the small-clause predicate first ('considered the most original her design') would need heavy-NP shift and is not natural here.

BAS2-31.note: Marginal: 'to repair the bridge it took the workers three months' (purpose-style fronting; it really wants a comma).

BAS2-35.note: 'The mail carrier kept barking at the neighbors' dog' is grammatical but absurd.

alternatives: my first summer job | always reminds | me | of | that song
BAS2-38.note: Swapping the NPs gives 'My first summer job always reminds me of that song', which is grammatical and natural.

BAS2-42.note: 'I' and 'the children' cannot swap because of 'was amazed' agreement and case.

BAS2-44.note: Marginal: 'for the whole family my grandmother used to sew dresses' (topicalization).
